prior_year_events.impact_description: Aggregate favourable development on prior accident years driven by lower frequencies (COVID-19 lockdown impact) and improved risk selection/product mix; calculated gross release of c.GBP 19.9m across older accident years

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate recorded net favourable prior-year reserve development in 2020. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates an aggregate gross release of approximately GBP 19.9m (c. -3.4% of opening gross claims outstanding), largely driven by lower claim frequencies during COVID-19 lockdowns and improved underwriting and risk selection; this was partially offset by ongoing claims cost inflation pressures noted in the report.
raw_causal_phrases: major improvement in net loss ratio (by 10.1%) ... reflecting the improvements made in risk selection and product mix, but predominantly from the benefits on claims frequencies due to the restrictions imposed to limit the spread of COVID-19 which reduced road and vehicle usage.
Claims frequencies fell dramatically during the first lockdown in March and April; and then again to a lesser extent in the second lockdown in November.
This offset higher claims costs where the increase in used car prices as new car sales have fallen is driving inflation in the cost of replacing written-off vehicles.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: The Movement-in-prior-years note in the accounts reports net releases (total net release GBP 18.163m) but does not show a gross prior-year movement. I derived the gross prior-year movement (-GBP 19.9m) from the gross claims development table (gross triangle) as the gross movement across underwriting years 2011-2018 (excluding the aggregate '2010 & prior' column). The triangle was used because the movement note provides only net figures. Values are rounded to one decimal place. Page references for notes/tables were inferred from the report pagination available in the source and may be approximate.
